sections.bio:
As a dedicated Artificial Intelligence undergraduate at Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Science & Technology (QUEST), I am passionate about applying AI and machine learning to solve meaningful, real-world problems. I thrive on learning new technologies and have hands-on experience with C, Java (OOP), and AI tools. 

I have completed several Coursera certifications, including Google Prompting Essentials and courses on designing effective AI prompts. My academic journey is complemented by a strong foundation in teamwork, problem solving, and self-motivation.

Recently, I developed EASY MED, a simple online platform for booking doctor appointments, aimed at making healthcare more accessible.

I am eager to further develop my skills through internships, research positions, and collaborative AI projects. I welcome opportunities to connect with professionals and organizations in the AI and data science space.

I used to think Linear Regression was just:
fit a line -> predict values -> done

But while practicing ML on Jupyter Notebook, I realized something important:

A model giving predictions doesn’t automatically mean the model is reliable.

That’s where the assumptions of Linear Regression come in.

Recently I learned about:
• linearity
• multicollinearity
• normal distribution of errors
• homoscedasticity
• No autocorelation of errors

And some of these names sounded scarier like homoscedasticity

The more I learn ML, the more I realize:
understanding the data and workflow matters just as much as understanding algorithms.

Still learning step by step through free resources, practice, mistakes, and lots of debugging 

Also sharing the video that helped me understand this topic better:
https://lnkd.in/dZTAVN2Y

Hiring in Pakistan is still painfully manual.
CVs screened by hand.
Decisions based on guesswork.
Bias slips into the process without anyone noticing.
So I built HireIQ — an AI-powered hiring assistant built for startups and SMEs.
What it does:
→ AI CV scoring with transparent explanations
→ Multi-candidate visual comparison
→ AI-generated interview questions
→ Bias detection for fair hiring
Built using React, FastAPI, Python, and Hugging Face.
Deployed. Live. Free to use.
Recently submitted it to the Transforming Enterprise Through AI Hackathon by Lablab.ai in collaboration with Google DeepMind and Gemini.

It was 1 AM. I was thinking about tomorrow's plans before sleeping.
Then a thought hit me: Why does every AI tool use just one model for everything?
I couldn't sleep after that.
By morning, Smart AI Expert was born — a multi-model AI router that actually thinks before answering:
🧠 Detects your intent in < 500ms 
⚡ Calls Groq + Cohere + OpenRouter in parallel 
🔀 Routes coding questions to the best code model
✍️ Routes creative tasks to the best creative model 
🧩 Combines all answers into one expert response
Sequential API calls were killing response times. So I parallelized everything with Python ThreadPoolExecutor.
Result: 6 seconds → 2 seconds. 3 models. 1 answer.
Stack: Flask · Docker · HuggingFace Spaces Budget: $0
Sometimes the best ideas come right before sleep. The trick is writing them down.
